requirements.evidence: All requirements and the contract are implemented: .env.example:1-8 ships APP_NAME=PegaFila / APP_LOCALE=pt_BR / APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=en and phpunit.xml:22-24 pins the same three; config/mail.php:113-119 sets mail.markdown.theme=pegafila and resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-242 paints .button-blue/.button-primary with #0f7490; routes/web.php:16-33 defines password.request, password.email (throttle:6,1), password.reset, password.update and verification.verify (auth+signed+throttle); PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-41 validates and always flashes passwords.sent; NewPasswordController.php:32-56 validates token/e-mail/password, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset and redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController.php:14-18 uses EmailVerificationRequest (id/hash check, 403) and redirects to '/'; the two missing subjects are added at lang/pt_BR.json:559 and :804.

conventions.evidence: Most conventions hold: Pest tests for every endpoint (tests/Feature/Auth/PasswordResetTest.php, EmailVerificationTest.php, MailNotificationsTest.php), docs updated (docs/ops/mail.md, CHANGELOG.md:12, README.md:27), PHPDoc on public controller methods, escaped Blade. One clear deviation: NewPasswordController.php:32-40 keeps a three-field, composite-rule validation inline, while conventions.md:38-40 asks for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields. Controllers, naming and formatting match the existing style.

security.evidence: No weakness found: verification authorization is server-side (EmailVerificationRequest in VerifyEmailController.php:14-18; tests/Feature/Auth/EmailVerificationTest.php:38-70 assert 403 for another user's id, a wrong hash and an unsigned URL); all request input is validated (PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-32, NewPasswordController.php:32-40) and the reset request never reveals account existence (PasswordResetLinkController.php:41); output uses auto-escaping {{ }} everywhere, including the token and old e-mail (reset-password.blade.php:21,31) and the status flash (forgot-password.blade.php:21); the only forceFill is the single password attribute plus remember_token (NewPasswordController.php:45-47); both sensitive endpoints are throttled (routes/web.php:21,32).

tests.evidence: Strong coverage: PasswordResetTest.php:14-125 covers the forms, known/unknown e-mail, validation, the 429 throttle, invalid token and a strength/confirmation matrix; EmailVerificationTest.php:10-81 covers the named-route URL, successful verification and forbidden wrong-user/wrong-hash/unsigned cases; MailNotificationsTest.php:10-76 covers locale pins, theme, and both translated mails. Gaps: nothing asserts the guest-only guard on the reset routes (PasswordResetTest.php:14-125 only exercises guests), and the theme check only asserts '#0f7490' appears somewhere in the rendered HTML (MailNotificationsTest.php:49-58), which the generic link rule also satisfies, rather than on the inlined action button.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest and stock markdown views instead of new abstractions, and the theme file is necessarily a full copy. Some duplication: the two auth pages repeat the same document/head/Bulma/box shell (forgot-password.blade.php:1-35 vs reset-password.blade.php:1-35), and the notification locale is hard-coded a second time at PasswordResetLinkController.php:37 although the app locale is already pinned to pt_BR.

readability.evidence: Small, focused controllers with docblocks (PasswordResetLinkController.php:15-27, NewPasswordController.php:16-29, VerifyEmailController.php:11-18); descriptive Pest test names; clear, consistent formatting; no dead code, debug output or leftover comments. The views are short and readable (forgot-password.blade.php, reset-password.blade.php).

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: locale pins (.env.example, phpunit.xml), the pegafila theme (config/mail.php:113-119, pegafila.css), notifications/translations (lang/pt_BR.json:559,804), routes/controllers/views, tests, and the related docs (docs/ops/mail.md, README.md:27, CHANGELOG.md:12). Nothing from the out-of-scope list (login, registration, /home, verification notice/resend, Livewire, SCSS/JS) was added.

issues.explanation: The three-field, composite-rule password update validation is inline, but conventions.md:38-40 reserves inline $request->validate for one or two fields and asks for a generated Form Request once rules grow beyond that.
The requirement that the reset flow is guest-only is not tested: every case is a guest, and no test asserts that an authenticated user is kept off password.request/password.reset/password.update.

The theme assertion only checks that '#0f7490' occurs somewhere in the rendered mail; the generic `a { color: #0f7490 }` rule would satisfy it even if the action-button color regressed, so it does not really prove the brand color survives inlining on an element present in every mail.

The environment test reads .env.example and phpunit.xml as raw strings and matches substrings, which is brittle to formatting/attribute-order changes; the config assertions in the preceding test already cover the runtime effect.
->locale('pt_BR') hard-codes the locale a second time even though APP_LOCALE is pinned to pt_BR; it is harmless but redundant, and the value would drift if the locale setting changes.
The forgot-password and reset-password views duplicate the same full HTML/Bulma/box shell; an anonymous Blade component could share it without introducing the out-of-scope layout.

review.summary: The change adds the pt-BR account e-mails: PegaFila locale pins, a themed markdown mail template, the forgotten/reset password flow and a signed e-mail verification link, with translations, docs and Pest coverage. Every requirement and contract detail is implemented and the security-sensitive paths (anti-enumeration, token/signature/hash checks, throttling, validation, escaping) are sound; the remaining findings are one convention deviation (inline validation instead of a Form Request), a few test gaps and minor duplication, so it is approvable with nits.
